fact: Remember when a 1GB SD card or USB flash drive felt bottomless and cost over $50?
Remember when 1GB of RAM on a smartphone was considered top-tier flagship spec?
Remember having to get off the internet because someone needed to make a phone call on the landline?
Remember spending hours customizing your MySpace profile with custom HTML, CSS, and auto-playing background music?
Remember taking 45 minutes to download a single MP3 on LimeWire, only for it to end up being a mislabeled audio clip?
Remember blowing into Nintendo cartridges or wiping scratched PS2 discs on your shirt to get games to load?
Remember rewinding VHS tapes before returning them to Blockbuster so you wouldn't get fined?
Remember how slow and relaxed days felt before infinite-scroll algorithmic feeds completely took over social media?
Remember carefully picking your top 8 MSN Messenger contacts or setting your status to custom song lyrics?
Remember carrying around a dedicated CD binder in your car or backpack just to listen to your music collection?
Remember when the anti-skip protection on portable CD players was a huge selling feature?
Remember T9 predictive texting on T9 keypads and how fast you could type without even looking at your screen?
Remember when Fruit Ninja, Angry Birds, and Temple Run were installed on literally every touch-screen phone?
Remember downloading custom polyphonic ringtones from TV commercials by texting a code to a 5-digit shortcode?
Remember waiting for the screen saver (like 3D Pipes or Flying Toasters) to kick in on Windows 95?
Remember when 800x600 and 1024x768 were standard desktop monitor resolutions?
Remember using Windows Movie Maker with blue background title cards and classic video transitions?
Remember burning a custom mix CD for a friend and carefully writing the tracklist on the disc with a Sharpie?
Remember using iTunes Cover Flow to swipe through album art in 3D?
Remember when skeuomorphic UI design meant notes apps looked like yellow legal pads and newsstand looked like real wood shelves?
Remember when Winamp was the ultimate music player and custom skins were a huge deal?
Remember the panic when someone accidentally bumped the table while your discman was playing?
Remember using Limewire, FrostWire, or Kazaa and constantly worrying about getting a computer virus?
Remember sliding open a Motorola RAZR or T-Mobile Sidekick and feeling like you were living in the future?
Remember floppy disks holding only 1.44 MB of data?
Remember buying video game cheat code books or printing out dozens of pages of walkthroughs from GameFAQs?
Remember when charging phones required micro-USB cables that only plugged in one way?
Remember spending hours decorating presentations with WordArt text effects and animated ClipArt?
Remember using a physical paper map or printing out step-by-step turn directions from MapQuest before going on a road trip?
Remember the distinct noise a computer speaker made right before your cell phone received an incoming text message?
Remember when Bluetooth file transfers between phones took several minutes for a single low-res image?
Remember taking photos on a disposable camera and having to wait days for the store to develop the film?
Remember feeding your Tamagotchi or Giga Pet throughout the school day so it wouldn't faint?
Remember jailbreaking your iPod Touch or iPhone just to get custom themes, dark mode, and free screen recorders?
Remember when computer monitors were massive, heavy CRT boxes that took up half your desk?
Remember keeping a plastic storage container full of cheat code sticky notes inside your Game Boy case?
Remember when Limewire download speeds were measured in kilobytes per second (KB/s)?
Remember playing Flash games on Miniclip, Newgrounds, and AddictingGames during computer lab classes?
Remember the screeching dial-up connection sound every time you logged onto AOL or EarthLink?
Remember when 16GB of internal storage on a smartphone meant you had to constantly delete photos and apps?
Remember Nudging your friends on MSN Messenger or sending Winks to shake their entire chat window?
Remember the thrill of finding a computer in the house that actually had 3D Pinball Space Cadet installed?
Remember using a worm light attachment on your Game Boy Color just to play games in the dark?
Remember when Webcams were external USB devices that sat on top of your monitor like small golf balls?
Remember BBM (BlackBerry Messenger) PINs being the ultimate way to stay connected with friends?
Remember organizing your digital music library by fixing artist names, genre tags, and track numbers manually in iTunes?
Remember using Encarta '95 or '98 on CD-ROM to look up info for school projects instead of using search engines?
Remember keeping a spare battery or AA batteries in your pocket so your portable device wouldn't die on the bus?
Remember when PC game boxes were huge, cardboard chests containing thick instruction manuals?
Remember when Instagram only let you post square-cropped photos with heavy vintage filters like Toaster or Earlybird?
Remember when blowing into the trackball of a computer mouse was required to clear out dust and dirt lint?
Remember having a limited text messaging plan and paying 10 cents per text message if you went over your limit?
Remember using USB flash drives shaped like wristbands, keychains, or mini sports cars?
Remember using Ask Jeeves or AltaVista before Google became the dominant search engine?
Remember downloading custom pointer cursors with trail effects for your Windows XP desktop?
Remember checking into places on Foursquare or Facebook just to become the 'Mayor' of your local coffee shop?
Remember downloading video clips in 240p or 360p resolution and thinking the quality was totally fine?
Remember renting a console game from video rental stores and praying the previous person didn't overwrite your save data?
Remember using P2P clients like eMule, BearShare, or Ares Galaxy to find obscure albums?
Remember the satisfaction of clicking a slide-out QWERTY keyboard into place on an early smartphone?
Remember when 720p HD video on YouTube felt like an absolute revolutionary upgrade over standard resolution?
Remember calling a dedicated weather line or theater hotline on your landline to check movie showtimes?
Remember setting up custom Away Messages on AIM (AOL Instant Messenger) with cool fonts and color themes?
Remember transferring songs onto a 128MB MP3 player that could only hold about 30 tracks at a time?
Remember the excitement of receiving free trial CDs for AOL in the mail containing 500 hours of free internet?
Remember spending hours playing Club Penguin, Habbo Hotel, or Webkinz after school?
Remember when phone displays were around 3.5 to 4 inches and easily operable with just one hand?
Remember using Windows Media Player visualizers on full screen while listening to ambient synth music?
Remember using physical TV Guide booklets to figure out what was airing on television tonight?
Remember pressing the web browser button on your flip phone by mistake and frantically mashing 'Cancel' so you wouldn't get charged data fees?
Remember customizing your Nokia phone with clip-on front plates and rubber button covers?
Remember using desktop widgets for weather, CPU usage clocks, and sticky notes on Windows 7?
Remember carrying a Game Boy, a transparent plastic game case cartridge holder, and extra AA batteries on family road trips?
Remember burning ISO images to CD-R or DVD-R discs using Nero Burning ROM or ImgBurn?
Remember when digital cameras had optical viewfinders and took AA batteries instead of rechargeable packs?
Remember watching the de-fragmentation animation on Windows 95/98 move color blocks around your hard drive?
Remember the satisfaction of snapping a clamshell flip phone shut to end a phone call?
Remember when portable power banks weren't common, so you had to hunt for wall outlets everywhere you went?
Remember the iconic startup sound of Windows XP and the crisp bliss of the default Bliss wallpaper landscape?
Remember using dial-up Internet after 9 PM because your ISP offered free evening minutes?
Remember when YouTube videos had a 10-minute length limit and no video monetization ads?
Remember installing Yahoo! Toolbar, Google Toolbar, or Ask Toolbar on Internet Explorer?
Remember when podcasts were audio files you had to manually sync to your iPod or MP3 player via iTunes overnight?
Remember storing video games on memory cards that only held 15 'blocks' of save data?
Remember when iPods used mechanical hard drives inside that spun up and clicked when loading songs?
Remember using RealPlayer or QuickTime to play web videos that buffered every 5 seconds?
Remember using physical phone books like the Yellow Pages to look up local store phone numbers and addresses?
Remember buying custom pre-made web banners or animated GIF icons for forum signatures?
Remember using web-based Flash games and dynamic Flash animations before Adobe phased out browser support?
Remember carrying both an iPod for music AND a cell phone for calls/texts everywhere you went?
Remember using a 3.5mm cassette tape adapter plugged into your portable CD player to play digital music in old car stereos?
Remember when YouTube's star rating system was 1 to 5 stars before it was simplified to Thumbs Up/Down?
Remember typing SMS messages using number keypads and pressing the '7' key four times just to get the letter 'S'?
Remember when 3G mobile data felt blazing fast compared to 2G/EDGE speeds?
Remember using the physical Turbo button on old computer cases to boost clock speeds?
Remember listening to low-bitrate 128kbps MP3s and thinking they sounded completely fine?
Remember using Sony Memory Stick PRO Duo cards or Olympus XD-Picture cards for digital cameras before SD cards became universal?
Remember waiting up late at night with a blank audio cassette tape queued up in your boombox, ready to press Record as soon as your favorite song played on the radio?
Remember when laptop battery life was under 2 hours and laptops generated enough heat to burn your lap?
Remember when 30-pin dock connector charging cables were huge and prone to tearing near the connector joint?
Remember having to manually clean the lint and rubber roller balls inside your computer mouse so the cursor wouldn't stutter?
Remember buying dedicated MP3 players like the Creative Zen or SanDisk Sansa and using mini-USB cables to sync audio files?
Remember using WinRAR or 7-Zip to extract multi-part split archives named '.part01.rar' and praying none of the chunks were corrupted?
Remember the distinctive smell of fresh laminated paper when opening a brand-new physical video game instruction booklet?
Remember when mobile phone screens were so dim in direct sunlight that you had to cup your hands over the display just to read a text message?
Remember downloading custom desktop pets or BonziBuddy, only to realize it was tracking your keyboard inputs?
Remember using physical landline caller ID boxes attached next to your home phone screen to see who was calling?
Remember when camera phones took images at 0.3 megapixels (VGA) and pictures looked completely pixelated on anything larger than a phone display?
Remember setting up custom custom HTML themes and flash widgets on early social networks like Orkut, Hi5, or Xanga?
Remember carrying a dedicated micro-USB car charger because phone batteries couldn't handle running GPS navigation for more than 45 minutes?
Remember keeping a rewinder machine shaped like a sports car specifically to rewind VHS tapes faster than your VCR could?
Remember playing games like Space Cadet Pinball, Solitaire, or Minesweeper during computer lab because the school firewall blocked all web browsers?
Remember the heartbreak when your optical CD-RW burner suffered a 'buffer underrun' error 99% through burning a disc, turning it into an unreadable coaster?
Remember using physical address books and home landline memory speed-dial buttons to call your friends after school?
Remember downloading custom skins for Windows Media Player, RealPlayer, or Yahoo! Messenger that completely reshaped the application window?
Remember when sliding capacitive touch screens didn't support multi-touch gestures, so pinching-to-zoom was impossible on early resistive screens?
Remember carefully sticking printed label stickers onto your home-burned CD-Rs so you could type custom title labels?
Remember adjusting the TV antenna or turning the dial on the back of portable CRT televisions to get rid of static scan lines?
Remember downloading polyphonic or monophonic ringtone keypress codes from magazine backpages and manually keying them into your phone's ringtone composer?
Remember when laptops featured built-in physical Wi-Fi toggle switches on the side casing to turn wireless networking on or off?
Remember the panic when your Game Boy screen began dimming and flickering because the four AA batteries were running out of juice?
Remember downloading custom launcher replacement apps on early Android versions just to get smooth 60fps home screen scrolling transitions?
Remember using physical infrared (IrDA) ports on mobile phones to beam business cards or tiny low-res MIDI files by holding the top edges together?
Remember listening to low-resolution audio streams over SHOUTcast internet radio inside Winamp or Windows Media Player?
Remember using physical floppy disk head cleaning kits with liquid drops to clean dusty drive heads on desktop PCs?
